pick_implementation.title: Pick the Tesla developer-app credential set
pick_implementation.description: Choose existing application credentials or add new ones. Add the same client_id / client_secret you registered for `tesla_fleet` — each integration goes through OAuth independently and gets its own refresh token, so they no longer rotate over each other.

region.title: Region
region.description: Tesla serves Fleet API accounts from regional endpoints. The region detected from your Tesla account is preselected — confirm it or correct it if needed.

vehicle.title: Select vehicle
vehicle.description: Choose the VIN this integration should track.

endpoint.title: Telemetry endpoint
endpoint.description:
Configure how Tesla reaches Home Assistant. The hostname must resolve publicly and present a TLS cert valid for the chain you'll put in `fleet_telemetry_config.ca`. The proxy secret is what nginx will inject as `X-Tesla-Proxy-Secret` on every forwarded request — copy it into your nginx config.

The partner private key is the EC P-256 (secp256r1) key whose public counterpart is hosted at `https://your-partner-domain/.well-known/appspecific/com.tesla.3p.public-key.pem`. If you don't have one yet, generate it with `openssl ecparam -genkey -name prime256v1 -noout -out partner.key` and paste the file contents below.

When adding another vehicle these fields are pre-filled from your existing setup — leave them unchanged unless your deployment moved.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Tesla
reauth_confirm.description: {name} needs a new Tesla authorization. This happens when “Allow vehicle commands” is on but the current authorization doesn't include the vehicle_cmds scope — continuing sends you to Tesla to grant it. Nothing else about the entry changes.

error.vin_not_found: That VIN is not on this account.
error.bad_key: Could not parse the private key. It must be a PEM-encoded private key.
error.wrong_curve: The key must be EC P-256 (curve secp256r1).

abort.missing_credentials: No application credentials configured. Add them via Settings → Devices & Services → Application Credentials.
abort.missing_configuration: Application credentials are missing. Add them and try again.
abort.no_url_available: No URL available for the OAuth callback. Configure an external URL or my.home-assistant.io.
abort.authorize_url_timeout: Timed out generating the authorize URL.
abort.authorize_url_fail: Could not generate the authorize URL.
abort.oauth_failed: Could not complete the OAuth flow.
abort.oauth_timeout: Timed out completing the OAuth flow.
abort.oauth_unauthorized: Tesla rejected the OAuth flow — the developer app may not be approved for the requested scopes.
abort.no_vehicles: Tesla returned no vehicles for this account.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach Tesla. Check network connectivity and try again.
abort.reauth_wrong_account: That Tesla account can't see this entry's vehicle. Sign in with the account that owns it.

init.title: Telemetry signals
init.description: Configure which signals the vehicle streams and how often. Each value is the minimum seconds between updates for that signal — Tesla emits on change and no more than once per interval, so it's a ceiling for high-churn signals, not a poll. Set a signal to 0 to disable it. Saving re-pushes the config to the car (no bootstrap needed). Leaving everything untouched keeps the built-in defaults.

driving.name: Driving & navigation
driving.description: Location, speed, gear, and active-route signals. 0 disables a signal.

battery.name: Battery & range
battery.description: State of charge and range estimates. 0 disables a signal.

charging.name: Charging
charging.description: Charge state, power/energy, cable, and limit signals. 0 disables a signal.

climate.name: Climate & cabin
climate.description: Cabin/outside temperature and HVAC signals. 0 disables a signal.

body.name: Body & security
body.description: Doors, windows, lock, and seat-occupancy signals. 0 disables a signal.

software.name: Software update
software.description: Update version and download/install progress. 0 disables a signal.

powertrain.name: Powertrain & thermal
powertrain.description: Drive-unit and battery-module temperatures. 0 disables a signal.

additional.name: Additional signals
additional.description: Signals you've added from the full catalog. 0 removes a signal.

add_signals.name: Add signals from the full Tesla catalog
add_signals.description: Pick any signal from the complete Tesla catalog to start streaming it; it appears above with its own interval next time you open this dialog. Note: a signal with no matching entity still streams and counts toward your signal bill, but surfaces only in the ‘Signals received’ breakdown.

cost.name: Signal cost estimate
cost.description: Tesla bills per streaming signal (one per data point). This rate drives the ‘Estimated signal cost’ sensor only — it does not change what Tesla charges. The default (≈ 6.67 per million) mirrors Tesla's published US rate of roughly $1 per 150,000 signals.

vehicle_commands.name: Vehicle commands
vehicle_commands.description: Off by default: the integration only reads telemetry. Turning this on enables the navigate service (sends a destination to the car) and, if the current authorization lacks the vehicle_cmds scope, starts a re-authentication that asks Tesla for it. Works only on vehicles that accept unsigned Fleet API commands (pre-2021 Model S/X).
